value: THE AFFORDANCE WAS THE DEFECT, NOT THE LOCK. The 2026-08-05 fix answered a bypass with three physics layers and every layer held; the corpus routed around them within two days because no reachable path could land a seal at all. What closed it was a required sink and a --seal flag — and, more than either, a non-sealing run that SAYS SO, because a run that printed green and persisted nothing was indistinguishable from one that sealed, which is how eight days of working around the door stayed invisible. THE PROOF WAS DEMANDING THE FALSE SENTENCE: test_a_FORCED_write_cannot_pass_for_a_seal asserted that standing()'s refusal contained 'recover the trail from git' — a remedy that never existed for that case (measured: the unlinked entries arrived unlinked at their first commit). A tooth can hold a lie in place through a whole voyage, and this one did. THREE CHART CLAIMS FALSIFIED BY THE BUILD'S OWN TOOL CALLS: survey said 'two production call sites' for run_proof (24 needed the sink, the rest in proofs/); survey measured 78 validation trails where the census reads 90; and hypothesis 8's expect proposed the snapshot 78 as the census floor while its own falsifier called that out — the falsifier was right and the expect was wrong, which is the useful direction for that pair to disagree in. THE PACKET'S SCORE, READ DOWNWARD (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap): 120 tool calls between the validate berth and done, against 50 for the whole seven-stage chart chain that produced it. Measured by timestamp against the session transcript, not estimated. Nothing counts this on its own — ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart is the owed observer — so the number is a hand's act and is recorded here rather than narrated. Three of the named falsifications above sit under it as the second layer: a score says the packet was thin, it never says which field was.

SUPERSEDED by a48f95c51a41 (PROVED 2026-08-16, Akien: 'the validation is a single record'): the trail link this watch counted retired with the chain at f745a4dd, and its probe was deleted there. Recorded by 693e9f45e6f2 (W2 child 1).

value.a: THE NARROWING IS NOT THE KILLED TOLERANCE, BY THAT RULE'S OWN TEST. The prior ticket's general shape is 'a tolerance is a forger's costume whenever the forger can produce the thing being tolerated.' It killed a tolerance of an unlinked leading PREFIX — and a forger can produce an unlinked prefix, since a total overwrite is one, which is why it fell. What is tolerated here is unlinked entries sitting BENEATH a newest link that verifies, and the forger cannot produce the required half: a link that hashes the current prefix comes only from the store's own _link_for, at which point calling the door is cheaper than forging. The rule and this narrowing agree.

THE DIAGNOSTIC IS NOT THE GATE, AND BOTH ARE KEPT. inspect_trail retains all three lanes and keeps checking the whole trail — it localizes a tamper to its earliest entry, which is what a census tooth should print and what complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass wants. Only standing()'s GATING question narrows. The instrument stays as sharp as it is; the gate stops answering a wider question than it was asked.

THE OLD-ENTRY-TAMPER CASE IS COVERED BY THE MERKLE PROPERTY, NOT BY THE TRAIL WALK. test_an_EDIT_to_an_older_entry_breaks_the_newest_link asserts breaks on entry 0 AND entry 1 — entry 1 being the newest — so the top link already catches it. The tooth's docstring claims the tamper is 'invisible to a newest entry reader'; that describes a reader of the newest RECORD's content, which is not what standing() will do.

WHAT WHOLE-TRAIL GATING ACTUALLY BOUGHT, stated so the loss is deliberate: localization of the earliest tamper point (kept — it moves to inspect_trail and the census tooth), and refusal on unlinked OLD entries (dropped on purpose — that is the class Akien ruled irrelevant once the point the evidence centred on is resolved).

THE QUARANTINE DESIGN IS WITHDRAWN AND WHY IT WAS WRONG BEYOND BEING UNNECESSARY. It would have written a ruling-shaped record into the trail permanently — a thing existing only because Akien signed it — at the moment the standing aim is to remove him from the process. 'I HAVE TO BE PART OF THE PROCESS. And we're trying slowly to remove me from the process' (Akien, 2026-08-16). The repointed gate needs no ruling at all, and that is a property of the fix worth naming, not a side effect.

standing()'s PRINTED REMEDY IS FALSE FOR THIS CLASS. It says 'Recover the trail from git and re-run the proof'; measured across every commit of test_host.json, entry 1 arrived unlinked at its first commit and carries no link at any commit. The sentence was written for the destroy-the-history attack and inherited by the never-came-through-the-door case. It is corrected as part of this ticket.
